findings.evidence: The only tab-switch scale proof is 'R2: switching tabs does not reconcile the 500-row Projects list', built from manyApps(50, 10) = 50 apps / 500 terminals, and it asserts only that stateOf is not re-read. No fixture uses the performance requirement's 300 apps / 3,000 terminals and nothing measures the 100 ms budget (no performance.now/Date.now around the switch), so a switch that took seconds at the stated size would still pass every test.
findings.description: The performance acceptance check for R10's tab switch - 300 apps and 3,000 terminals, panel update under 100 ms - has no test at that size and no timing assertion at all.

findings.evidence: The long-name test only asserts the Up and Show hidden buttons are present and that the title attribute holds the full 'context / folder' text. It never asserts the truncation CSS (.context/.folder text-overflow: ellipsis, .action flex: none), so removing the ellipsis or letting the title grow would not fail any test.
findings.description: The edge case 'truncated without hiding the Up and Show hidden controls' is proven for the DOM controls but not for the layout that actually keeps them visible; a CSS-module assertion like the R2 strip tests would close it.

findings.evidence: The amber case feeds t1=running and t2=stopping, which is already amber from the 'some up' branch, so the 'or stopping' clause is never exercised on its own. A projectsRollup that dropped stopping-only states would still pass this suite.
findings.description: The 'or stopping' half of the R7 amber rule has no independent test (e.g. all-stopping/stopped with no running terminal).
